summary: The build is on track for Botswana (30 November to 3 December). The walkthrough on 11 November went well and the WhatsApp payment card is in place. Your step-by-step guide is ready, and we meet again on Wednesday 18 November.

updates.text: Your privacy policy page is live on your website, and Naidene is named as the Information Officer. Thank you, Grant. This is what Meta needs before WhatsApp can be switched on for real.

Your step-by-step guide is ready: a tap-through tutorial with pictures of every screen, short quizzes, and a section to test the app on your iPad. It is on this page under "Your step-by-step guide" and uses the same password. It shows practice data only.

Thank you for the walkthrough feedback. We are improving the look of the login page and shortening the wordy screens. We are also adding a "Send by SMS instead" button, so if a WhatsApp message does not arrive, your team can resend it by SMS with one tap.

Walkthrough done and the company card is added in Meta. Thank you, Naidene. Until the event, Deon is your contact on +27 73 302 0683 in normal business hours. From 30 November to 3 December there will be standby cover from 07:00 to 20:00, and we will tell you the standby person's name and number before the event.
Confirmed: guests arriving on 30 November are checked in that day. Accreditation days stay 1, 2 and 3 December.
The card step moves to Wednesday 11 November, straight after the walkthrough. Naidene, you stay on the same call. Deon will show you Meta's rates on screen, with a rough total for 300 guests.

We received your signed page of the data agreement, thank you. Deon will countersign and send you the completed copy. A practice version of the platform is set up for the walkthrough, with invented names only and nothing sent to anyone.

Your new WhatsApp number (+27 71 472 5395) is connected to your Melted Workx business account, and Meta has approved "Melted Workx" as the name guests will see. Thank you for standing by with the phone.

Your question about keeping guest details longer: yes, partly. With each guest's agreement, basic contact details (name, organisation, email, WhatsApp number and language) can be kept for future events. Passport copies and dietary and accessibility details are still deleted after each event. This is noted for after Botswana, and nothing changes for Botswana.

Your new WhatsApp number works on the borrowed phone, so no eSIM change is needed and your own phone stays as it is. Your Melted Workx business account is set up on Meta, with you invited as an admin. The data agreement has been emailed to you for signature. Shuttle messages will use a simple shuttle list that Lez uploads.
Your website is live with everything Meta needs. Thank you, Grant.
Walkthrough booked for Wednesday 11 November at 10:00 on Google Meet. Grant is needed for the first 20 minutes only.

Both Botswana registration forms are ready, approved by OSF, with the tick box for travel messages. Local guests will not be messaged, so their form stays as it is. SMS messages will go through Clickatell, a South African provider.
Agreed: guests register for Botswana on your Google Form as usual, with one added tick box so they agree to receive WhatsApp and SMS messages about their travel.

Received your iPad details, your company documents for the WhatsApp approval, your Cape Town shuttle list and the headings of your registration sheet. For practice we use a scrambled copy of the Cape Town list, so no real guest details are shared.
Cape Town dates received (14 to 19 November). We will use them for a quiet practice run alongside your own process.
Event dates received: Botswana, 30 November to 3 December, with accreditation on 1, 2 and 3 December. Logos received. Manual check-in by name, without a scan, is planned for the day.
Project approved. Planning complete and the build team is set up. Registration and event setup come first.

questions.q: Can we keep guest data longer than one year, so returning OSF guests don't have to give their details again?
questions.a: Yes, partly. With each guest's agreement, we can keep name, organisation, email, WhatsApp number and language for future events. Passport copies and dietary and accessibility details are still deleted after each event, because the law treats them as sensitive. Please check with OSF that they are happy for Melted Workx to keep their delegates' details. After Botswana, Deon will send a short proposal for a returning-guest list, with a small update to the data agreement.

questions.q: How much will Meta charge for the WhatsApp messages?
questions.a: Meta charges a small amount for each WhatsApp message that is delivered, depending on the guest's country. Your card pays only these charges, and nothing is sent until messages are switched on. For Botswana the rate per message is a fraction of a rand, so for about 300 guests the total is expected to be small. Deon will confirm the exact rate from your WhatsApp Manager and send you a rough total. SMS messages are charged at cost from a prepaid balance, and we only send them with your say-so.
